queries: How should fresh basil be stored so that it does not wilt?
documents: During a storm the keeper trimmed the wick, wound the clockwork that turned the lens, sounded the fog signal and logged every passing ship until the weather cleared.
Neptune has the fastest winds measured on any planet: gusts in its upper atmosphere exceed two thousand kilometres per hour, far stronger than any storm on Earth.

repeated_documents.text: Basil is a warm-weather herb that dislikes the cold of a refrigerator, where its leaves darken within a day. Treat the bunch like cut flowers instead: trim a centimetre from each stem, remove the lowest leaves, and stand the stems in a jar with a few centimetres of water. Keep the jar on the kitchen counter, out of direct sunlight, and change the water every second day. A loose plastic bag over the leaves slows wilting without trapping too much moisture. Picked this way, basil stays fragrant for about a week.
